route_idioms.framework: Django URLconf (django.urls.re_path / django.conf.urls.include) + Django REST Framework class-based endpoints
route_idioms.how_declared: Routes are only declared with re_path(regex, view, name=...). A search found no bare django path() calls in src/. The root is ROOT_URLCONF = "sentry.conf.urls" (src/sentry/conf/server.py:416). That module re-exports urlpatterns from sentry.web.urls (src/sentry/conf/urls.py:3). The view is either `SomeEndpoint.as_view()` (a DRF Endpoint subclass) or a plain function. The HTTP methods are not in the URLconf: they come from the methods defined on the endpoint class (`def get` / `def post` / `def put` / `def delete`), and the `publish_status = {"POST": ...}` dict repeats them. Endpoint classes carry silo decorators: @internal_cell_silo_endpoint, @cell_silo_endpoint or @control_silo_endpoint. The path syntax is a Python regex string. It is anchored with ^, usually ends with /$, and names its parameters as `(?P<name>[^/]+)` (sometimes `\d+`, `\w+`, `.+`, or a constrained alternation). Some patterns contain non-capturing alternations such as `(?:issues|groups)` or `(?:notes|comments)`, so one pattern matches several literal paths. Optional pieces appear as `/?$` and `(?:...)?`. The route `name=` is significant: other code builds URLs from it with django.urls.reverse().

route_idioms.prefix_rules:
Full path = the concatenation of every enclosing re_path regex, each stripped of its leading ^ and with the trailing $ only on the leaf. The include forms are:
(1) include("dotted.module"). The string names a module whose `urlpatterns` is used. Examples: src/sentry/web/urls.py:183-184 r"^api/0/" -> include("sentry.api.urls"); src/sentry/web/urls.py:1335 r"^extensions/" -> include([... r"^github/" (1364) -> include("sentry.integrations.github.urls") ...]).
(2) include([...inline list...]). Examples: src/sentry/web/urls.py:204 r"^oauth/"; src/sentry/api/urls.py:2780 scim/v2; src/sentry/api/urls.py:2839 profiling.
(3) include(MODULE_LEVEL_VAR). The variable names a list literal in the same file. In src/sentry/api/urls.py:3809-3977: r"^relays/" -> RELAY_URLS (3812-3813), r"^organizations/" -> ORGANIZATION_URLS (1414), r"^projects/" -> PROJECT_URLS (2942), plus TEAM_URLS, USER_URLS, SENTRY_APP_URLS, AUTH_URLS, BROADCAST_URLS, r"^internal/" -> INTERNAL_URLS (3695), RELOCATION_URLS. AUTH_V2_URLS is imported from src/sentry/auth_v2/urls.py (api/urls.py:94).
(4) Splatting lists from other modules into a list literal: *preprod_urls.preprod_organization_urlpatterns (api/urls.py:2939), *preprod_urls.preprod_project_urlpatterns (3528), *preprod_urls.preprod_internal_urlpatterns (3790), *notification_platform_urls.internal_urlpatterns (3791), *workflow_urls.organization_urlpatterns (2928). These come from `from sentry.preprod.api.endpoints import urls as preprod_urls` (api/urls.py:520) and similar imports; the lists are defined in src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/urls.py:89/153/264 and src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/urls.py:25.
(5) A function that generates a list: include(create_group_urls(name_prefix, is_legacy_path=...)), defined at src/sentry/api/urls.py:947. It is mounted at r"^(?:issues|groups)/" (3817-3818) and at org-scoped r"^(?P<organization_id_or_slug>[^/]+)/(?:issues|groups)/" (1426-1427). Route names inside it are f-strings (f"{name_prefix}-group-details").
(6) Conditional `urlpatterns += [...]` guarded by settings: debug_urls when DEBUG_VIEWS (web/urls.py:89-92), media serving (98-107) with a regex built at runtime as rf"^{re.escape(settings.MEDIA_URL...)}...", and r"^manage/" when SENTRY_MODE != SAAS (118-125).
Example of a fully resolved cross-service path: /api/0/relays/projectconfigs/ = web/urls.py:183 "api/0/" + api/urls.py:3812 "relays/" + api/urls.py:1250 "projectconfigs/".

route_idioms.how_declared: Browser routes for the React app are not HTTP API routes. On the Django side many of them fall through to react_page_view or GenericReactPageView, for example src/sentry/web/urls.py:118-125 and the org/issue patterns near line 1417. None of these are called by relay, snuba or symbolicator, so the answer key can ignore them.

client_idioms.library: urllib3 HTTPConnectionPool via sentry.net.http.connection_from_url (Snuba client)
client_idioms.how_url_is_built: A module-level pool is bound to the Snuba base URL: `_snuba_pool = connection_from_url(settings.SENTRY_SNUBA, ...)` (src/sentry/utils/snuba.py:590-603). Every call is `_snuba_pool.urlopen(METHOD, path, body=..., headers=...)` with a path relative to the host. The path is usually an f-string whose segments are known only at runtime (dataset, entity, storage name, protobuf class name and version). snuba_rpc imports the same pool (src/sentry/utils/snuba_rpc.py:56). The RPC path is f"/rpc/{endpoint_name}/{class_version}", where endpoint_name = req.__class__.__name__ and class_version = cls.__module__.split(".", 3)[2]. Both come from the sentry_protos message class, for example EndpointTraceItemTable/v1 (snuba_rpc.py:400-401, 520-521). The batch path hardcodes the names "EndpointTraceItemTable" and "EndpointTimeSeries" (163-167).
client_idioms.base_url_config: settings.SENTRY_SNUBA = os.environ.get("SNUBA", "http://127.0.0.1:1218") (src/sentry/conf/server.py:1784); timeout SENTRY_SNUBA_TIMEOUT = 30 (server.py:1785).
examples: src/sentry/utils/snuba.py:1587 _snuba_pool.urlopen("POST", f"/{request.dataset}/snql", body=body, headers=headers)  -> Snuba POST /{dataset}/snql

(method and url passed by keyword through local variables)

client_idioms.library: django.urls.reverse() + internal URL prefix, passed as data to Symbolicator (Symbolicator calls back into Sentry)
client_idioms.how_url_is_built: Sentry does not make this request itself. It builds absolute URLs to its own routes and puts them in the JSON body sent to Symbolicator as a source of "type": "sentry" together with a system token. Symbolicator then calls Sentry. The URL is get_internal_url_prefix() + reverse(<route name>, kwargs={org, project}). The prefix comes from the system.internal-url-prefix option or system.url-prefix (src/sentry/lang/native/sources.py:325-342). This builds a reverse edge symbolicator -> sentry, and it can only be resolved by matching the route name used in reverse() to name= in the URLconf.
client_idioms.base_url_config: options system.internal-url-prefix, falling back to system.url-prefix (src/sentry/lang/native/sources.py:330-332)

extractor_notes:
INTER-SERVICE EDGES FOUND FROM SENTRY'S SIDE (the answer-key candidates)
(1) relay -> sentry. Sentry serves /api/0/relays/{register/challenge, register/response, projectconfigs, publickeys, live, <relay_id>}/. The path composes from web/urls.py:183 + api/urls.py:3812 + RELAY_URLS at api/urls.py:1238-1269. Methods: POST for challenge, response, projectconfigs and publickeys; GET for live. Sentry 404s /api/relay/.* (web/urls.py:144) and no longer serves the ingest routes (store, envelope). Those live in relay.
(2) sentry -> snuba. POST /{dataset}/snql, POST /{dataset}/mql, DELETE /{storage}, POST /rpc/{EndpointClassName}/{version}, POST and DELETE /{dataset}/{entity}/subscriptions[/{id}]. Test and dev only: /tests/{entity}/eventstream, /tests/entities/{entity}/insert, /tests/entities/eap_items/insert_bytes, /tests/{dataset}/drop.
(3) sentry -> symbolicator. POST /symbolicate, /symbolicate-js, /symbolicate-jvm, /symbolicate-any, /minidump, /applecrashreport. GET /requests/{task_id}.
(4) symbolicator -> sentry, via URLs that Sentry passes in the payload. GET /api/0/projects/{org}/{project}/files/dsyms/ (with ?id=) and /api/0/projects/{org}/{project}/artifact-lookup/ (with ?download=).
(5) sentry -> relay, tests only. /api/{project_id}/store|security|minidump|unreal/{key}|events/{id}/attachments/ and /api/relay/healthcheck/ready/.

EASY (single-file, tree-sitter-local)
- Leaf re_path(r"...", X.as_view(), name="...") calls. Read the first string argument (a raw string; remember the r prefix), the view class from the attribute call `.as_view()`, and the name= keyword.
- HTTP methods. Find the class named in as_view() and collect its method_definitions named get/post/put/patch/delete/head/options. The keys of `publish_status = {...}` give the same answer. Resolving the class needs the import map of urls.py, which has thousands of `from x import Y` lines, but that is a mechanical lookup.
- Nesting with an inline include([...]) list, and include(VAR) where VAR is a module-level list literal in the same file (RELAY_URLS, ORGANIZATION_URLS, PROJECT_URLS, INTERNAL_URLS). Walk the assignment and concatenate the prefixes.
- Regex-to-template normalisation. Strip ^ and $. Turn (?P<name>...) into {name}. Turn `/?` into `/`. Expand (?:a|b) into one route per alternative. Mark .* and .+ tails as wildcards. Use a real regex parser for this: the patterns contain nested parentheses inside named groups, for example event_id at api/urls.py:~967.
- Snuba and Symbolicator call sites whose path argument is a string literal: "/tests/entities/group_attributes/insert", "symbolicate", "symbolicate-js", "/rpc/EndpointTraceItemTable/v1".
- Concatenations of the form settings.SENTRY_SNUBA + "literal". The left operand identifies the service; the right operand is the path.

NEEDS CROSS-FILE RESOLUTION
- include("dotted.module.path"). Resolve the module to a file and read its `urlpatterns` (the integrations, for example web/urls.py:1364 -> src/sentry/integrations/github/urls.py:7).
- ROOT_URLCONF (conf/server.py:416) -> sentry.conf.urls, which re-exports sentry.web.urls.urlpatterns (conf/urls.py:3). You need this re-export to find the root.
- Splatted lists from imported modules: *preprod_urls.preprod_project_urlpatterns and others at api/urls.py:2928/2939/3528/3790/3791. Follow the module alias (`import ... urls as preprod_urls`) to the attribute's list literal. The splat inherits the enclosing include's prefix (organizations/, projects/, internal/).
- AUTH_V2_URLS is imported from sentry.auth_v2.urls (api/urls.py:94).
- create_group_urls(...) at api/urls.py:947. It is a function that returns list literals, and route names are f-strings. Evaluate the function body's returned lists and substitute name_prefix. It is mounted twice, at 1426 and 3818.
- Constants used as paths: EAP_ITEMS_INSERT_ENDPOINT, defined in sentry/utils/eap.py:2 and imported into eventstream/snuba.py, replays/lib/eap/write.py and testutils. The class attribute snuba_endpoint = "/tests/entities/{entity}/insert" (testutils/cases.py:1544) is used through cls.snuba_endpoint.format(...).
- Base-URL identity for pools. `_snuba_pool` is defined once in utils/snuba.py:590 from settings.SENTRY_SNUBA and imported elsewhere: `from sentry.utils.snuba import _snuba_pool`, or used as snuba._snuba_pool. Track the binding variable -> base-setting -> service across imports and module attributes. snuba_transpiler.py:393 creates a separate local pool from the same setting. Settings values live in conf/server.py: SENTRY_SNUBA at 1784, the symbolicator URL at 2821, plus options/defaults.py:517. Map these setting names to services: SENTRY_SNUBA/SNUBA -> snuba (default port 1218); symbolicator.options/SYMBOLICATOR_POOL_URLS -> symbolicator (port 3021).
- Symbolicator wrapper chain. Symbolicator._process(task, path) -> SymbolicatorSession.create_task(path) -> _request("post", path) -> urljoin(self.url, path) -> session.request(method, url). The literal path is two or three calls away from the actual requests call. The extractor must treat `_process`'s second argument (or create_task's first) as the endpoint, and treat the class as bound to the symbolicator base URL. Method strings are lowercase ("post", "get").
- Reverse edges through django reverse(). sources.py:351 and :381 build URLs from route names, and those URLs are handed to symbolicator in JSON. Resolving them needs the global route-name -> composed path index built from the URLconf (name="sentry-api-0-dsym-files" -> /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/files/dsyms/). The caller is really Symbolicator's 'sentry' source downloader, so model this as a symbolicator -> sentry edge whose evidence sits in sentry. Hybrid-cloud RPC uses reverse("sentry-api-0-rpc-service") the same way (hybridcloud/rpc/service.py:563), but that is sentry -> sentry.
- Test fixtures whose URLs are built inside pytest fixture closures and injected as attributes (testutils/pytest/relay.py:299-341 -> testutils/relay.py:186-204 -> self.get_relay_store_url(...) at testutils/relay.py:63). Static resolution requires following the fixture name to the attribute assignment and then to the closure's .format template.

ONLY KNOWABLE AT RUNTIME (best case: emit a parameterised template)
- Snuba dataset, entity and storage segments: f"/{request.dataset}/snql", f"/{query.storage_name}", f"/{snuba_query.dataset}/{entity_key.value}/subscriptions". Emit /{dataset}/snql and similar, and let the matcher unify them with snuba's own parameterised routes.
- The Snuba RPC endpoint name and version come from the protobuf request class: cls.__name__ and cls.__module__.split(".", 3)[2] (snuba_rpc.py:400-401, 520-521). Emit /rpc/{name}/{version}. Only the hardcoded "EndpointTraceItemTable"/"EndpointTimeSeries" (snuba_rpc.py:163-167) and "/rpc/EndpointTraceItemTable/v1" (snuba_transpiler.py:388) are concrete.
- The Symbolicator base URL is chosen per pool from settings or options at runtime (symbolicator.py:134-143). urljoin semantics mean a base URL with a path component but no trailing slash would replace the last segment. Statically, assume the paths sit at the root.
- The internal URL prefix for the reverse() source URLs comes from runtime options (sources.py:325-342), and the query strings ?_last_upload= and ?download= are appended dynamically.
- Routes added conditionally on settings (DEBUG_VIEWS, SERVE_UPLOADED_FILES, SENTRY_MODE at web/urls.py:89-125). The MEDIA_URL route regex is built with rf"^{re.escape(settings.MEDIA_URL...)}" (web/urls.py:101). Mark these as conditional or skip them.
- The test Relay URL port is a docker runtime value (pytest/relay.py:180).

LIKELY MISSES AND FALSE-POSITIVE RISKS
- Lists built with `urlpatterns += [...]` across if-blocks. The extractor must merge these augmented assignments, not just read the first assignment.
- Catch-all routes r"^" (CatchallEndpoint, api/urls.py:4009-4011) and pattern r"^(?P<organization_slug>[^/]+)/..." on the web side match almost anything. Rank exact matches above them, or exclude them, when matching inbound calls.
- Hundreds of connection_from_url pools point at Seer, the profiling service and others. Without base-setting resolution they would be mislabelled as snuba. Integration clients (base_url = "https://api.github.com" and similar) and safe_urlopen of user URLs are external, not inter-service.
- mock.patch strings like "sentry.utils.snuba_rpc._snuba_pool.urlopen" in tests are not calls. Ignore string occurrences inside mock.patch.
- Relay sends query strings such as ?version=3 to projectconfigs. Sentry's route regex has no query part, so strip query strings before matching.

route_idioms.how_declared: Routes are method-chained calls on `Router::new()`: `.route(PATH, METHOD_ROUTER)`. Every top-level route is in relay-server/src/endpoints/mod.rs, inside the functions `internal_routes` (L54-60), `public_routes` (L65-68) and `public_routes_raw` (L71-138). METHOD_ROUTER takes one of two forms. It can be inline, as in `get(health_check::handle)`, `post(...)` or `any(...)` (imported from axum::routing at L33). Or it can be a call to a per-endpoint factory such as `store::route(config)`, which returns `MethodRouter<ServiceState>`. In the factory case the HTTP verb is only visible inside the factory body in the endpoint file. Examples: `post(handle)`; `post(handle_post).get(handle_get)` (store.rs:157); `on(MethodFilter::GET.or(MethodFilter::POST), handle)` (monitor.rs:81); `patch(handle_patch)` / `axum_head(handle_head)` (upload.rs:62-70). Path params use brace syntax `{name}`, and catch-alls use `{*name}`. Trailing-slash variants are registered as separate duplicate .route calls.
route_idioms.prefix_rules:
There is no global prefix: each top-level path is an absolute literal starting with /api/.

Composition rules:
- `.merge(r)` unions routers with no prefix (mod.rs:47, 132-135).
- `.nest(PREFIX, sub::routes(config))` prepends PREFIX to the literals of a sub-router defined in another file (mod.rs:120-122). Example: `/api/{project_id}/integration/otlp` + `/v1/traces` (otlp.rs:25) gives `/api/{project_id}/integration/otlp/v1/traces`.
- A path can be a const imported from another module: `.route(UPLOAD_PATCH_PATH, ...)` at mod.rs:106-107. The const is defined at services/upload.rs:48 as `/api/{project_id}/upload/{key}/`.

Conditional routes:
- `#[cfg(sentry)]` adds the playstation route (mod.rs:109-110).
- Integration routes exist only when `RelayMode::Managed`; Proxy mode uses an empty Router (mod.rs:117-126).

Fallback and serving:
- `.fallback(forward::forward)` (mod.rs:137) proxies any other /api/ path to the upstream.
- The routers are served by services/server/mod.rs:208-217. With an internal listener, public_routes and internal_routes go on two ports; otherwise all_routes is served.
- They are wrapped in NormalizePath (middlewares/normalize_path.rs:37-44), which collapses duplicate slashes before routing.
examples: relay-server/src/endpoints/mod.rs:91-94 .route("/api/{project_id}/cron/{monitor_slug}/{sentry_key}", monitor::route(config)) (+ trailing-slash and no-sentry_key variants) -> monitor.rs:81 on(GET|POST)

relay-server/src/endpoints/mod.rs:106-107 .route(UPLOAD_PATCH_PATH, upload::route_patch(config)) / .route(UPLOAD_PATCH_PATH, upload::route_head()); const at relay-server/src/services/upload.rs:48 = "/api/{project_id}/upload/{key}/"
relay-server/src/endpoints/mod.rs:137 .fallback(forward::forward) -> forward.rs:43 only /api/* (excluding exactly /api/) is proxied upstream, gated by config http_forward

client_idioms.library: Relay's internal UpstreamRelay service, built on reqwest::Client: the trait objects UpstreamRequest and UpstreamQuery
client_idioms.how_url_is_built:
Relay sends no URLs from call sites. A request is a struct that implements one of two traits:
- `UpstreamRequest`: a raw request (trait at services/upstream.rs:378-389).
- `UpstreamQuery`: a JSON-body, signed query (trait at services/upstream.rs:494-510).

The struct provides `fn method(&self) -> Method` and `fn path(&self) -> Cow<str>`, which return the verb and a path relative to the upstream. It is sent with `upstream_relay.send(SendRequest(x))` or `upstream_relay.send(SendQuery(x))`. UpstreamQueryRequest delegates path and method to the query (upstream.rs:613-618).

The single place a URL is built is UpstreamRelay `build_request`, at services/upstream.rs:931-936:
`request.upstream().unwrap_or_else(|| config.upstream()).get_url(request.path())`
followed by `self.reqwest.request(request.method(), url)`.

`UpstreamDescriptor::get_url` (relay-config/src/upstream.rs:77-80) is `format!("{self}{}", path.trim_start_matches('/'))`, which joins scheme://host:port/ with the path.

Paths are mostly string literals returned via Cow::Borrowed or `.into()`. Two are format! strings that interpolate project_id. Two are fully dynamic: the forward proxy passes the incoming URI through, and the upload PATCH/HEAD reuses a stored Location uri.
client_idioms.base_url_config: Base URL is the `relay.upstream` config key: `pub upstream: UpstreamDescriptor` (relay-config/src/config.rs:497). It defaults to https://sentry.io/ (relay-config/src/config.rs:551 and relay-config/src/upstream.rs:104) and is read through Config::upstream() (config.rs:2209). Local dev sets it in devservices/config/relay.yml:3 as `upstream: "http://host.docker.internal:8001/"`, which is the Sentry web server. A per-request override is possible via `fn upstream() -> Option<&UpstreamDescriptor>` (for example SendEnvelope.upstream, ForwardRequest .with_upstream(None)). The upstream is either Sentry or another Relay, so the target service can only be known at runtime/config time.

extractor_notes:
ROUTES (tree-sitter-rust)

Easy:
- Match `call_expression` where the function is a `field_expression` whose field is `route`, and the first argument is a `string_literal`. All top-level paths are absolute literals in one file (relay-server/src/endpoints/mod.rs).
- Treat `{x}` and `{*x}` as params.
- Normalize duplicate trailing-slash variants (e.g. otlp.rs:25-28, mod.rs:91-94, 101-102) into one route, or keep both.
- The verb is easy when the second arg is an inline call `get|post|any(...)` (mod.rs:56-83).

Needs cross-file resolution:
(1) The verb, when the second arg is `module::route(config)` / `route_post` / `route_patch` / `route_head`.
- Resolve the function in endpoints/<module>.rs.
- Read the method-router expression it returns: `post(..)`, `post(..).get(..)` chains, `patch`, `axum_head` (an alias for `head` via `use ... head as axum_head`, upload.rs:14), and `on(MethodFilter::GET.or(MethodFilter::POST), ..)` (monitor.rs:81).
- A fallback is to emit the route with method ANY.
(2) `.nest(PREFIX_LITERAL, integrations::X::routes(config))`.
- Follow to endpoints/integrations/X.rs.
- Concatenate PREFIX with each inner `.route` literal.
- The sub-router's `routes` fn uses `axum::Router::new()` fully qualified.
(3) `.route(UPLOAD_PATCH_PATH, ..)`: resolve a `const` imported via `use crate::services::upload::UPLOAD_PATCH_PATH` (mod.rs:38) to services/upload.rs:48.
(4) Router variables.
- `let web_routes = Router::new()...; ... .merge(web_routes)`, plus shadowing (`let store_routes = store_routes.route(...)`, mod.rs:110-111).
- `.merge` adds no prefix, so collecting every .route in the file is sufficient.
- It is also safe to ignore `route_layer`, `match config.relay_mode()` arms, and `#[cfg(sentry)]` attributes. Optionally tag those routes conditional (Managed-mode only / sentry cfg).

Runtime only:
- `.fallback(forward::forward)` serves arbitrary /api/* paths by proxying them. Model it as a catch-all `/api/{*path}` proxy edge rather than a concrete route.
- Which listener (public vs internal port) serves a router depends on config (services/server/mod.rs:207-217).
- Ignore `.merge(` / `.route(` hits outside endpoints/: rate_limits.merge, upstream.rs `request.route()`, and the matchit::Router::new() in services/upload.rs:1023 are not HTTP route declarations. Scope the extractor to receivers built from `Router::new()` / `axum::Router::new()`.

CLIENT CALLS

Pattern:
- There are no URL strings at call sites. The extractor must find `impl UpstreamRequest for T` and `impl UpstreamQuery for T` blocks.
- Within each block, read `fn method` (returns `Method::POST`, `reqwest::Method::POST`, or a match on an enum) and `fn path` (returns `Cow::Borrowed("...")`, `"...".into()`, or `format!(...)`).
- Pair them as one outbound call. Call sites are `.send(SendRequest(T{..}))` / `.send(SendQuery(T{..}))`, which only matter for linking the caller function.

Path handling:
- Easy literal paths: GetProjectStates, GetGlobalConfig, GetRelays, RegisterRequest, RegisterResponse, GetHealthCheck, SendMetricsRequest.
- Strip query strings (`?version=3`).
- format! paths (SendEnvelope `/api/{}/envelope/`, UploadRequest Create `/api/{project_id}/upload/`): convert `{}` / `{ident}` placeholders into wildcard params.
- Fully dynamic paths: UploadRequest Upload/Head (uri from a stored Location built at upload.rs:857), ForwardRequest::builder(method, uri.to_string()) (forward.rs:47).
- ForwardRequest::builder with literal paths (register.rs:11, :23) is easy: treat the builder's second arg as the path and its first arg as the verb.

Base URL:
- Never in code. It is always config `relay.upstream` (default https://sentry.io/; devservices/config/relay.yml:3 points to the Sentry web server at host.docker.internal:8001).
- An extractor should hard-code the rule 'relay upstream = sentry (or another relay)'. Matching then works by path only against sentry's routes.
- Sentry composes these routes as api/0/ (src/sentry/web/urls.py:183) + ^relays/ (src/sentry/api/urls.py:3812) + RELAY_URLS (urls.py:1238-1269).

Answer-key edges (relay -> sentry), which match by path:
- POST /api/0/relays/projectconfigs/ (projects/source/upstream.rs:81, global_config.rs:88)
- POST /api/0/relays/publickeys/ (relays.rs:108)
- POST /api/0/relays/register/challenge/ (upstream.rs:851, register.rs:11)
- POST /api/0/relays/register/response/ (upstream.rs:875, register.rs:23)
- GET /api/0/relays/live/ (upstream.rs:808)

Calls with no sentry match (relay-to-relay or a self-call; exclude from cross-service edges):
- /api/0/relays/metrics/ (bucket.rs:736)
- /api/{id}/envelope/ (common.rs:273)
- /api/{id}/upload/ and /upload/{key}/ (upload.rs:1176, 857)
- /api/relay/healthcheck/{mode}/ (relay/src/healthcheck.rs:32)

Other notes:
- I found no relay code that calls snuba or symbolicator over HTTP.
- objectstore_client (services/objectstore.rs:506) goes to objectstore, which is not one of the four repos.
- Relay's outcomes and processing output go over Kafka, not HTTP.
- The glob strings in endpoints/forward.rs:70-79 (`/api/0/projects/*/*/releases/*/files/`, `/api/0/organizations/*/chunk-upload/`) only set body-size limits for the forward proxy. They are not outbound calls, though they hint at sentry routes that are proxied at runtime.
- The tests/ directory holds Python integration tests that call relay. They are test-only and should be excluded.

route_idioms.framework: Flask (Werkzeug routing), public query API app `snuba.web.views:application`
route_idioms.how_declared: A single module-level `application = Flask(__name__, static_url_path="")` object (snuba/web/views.py:128). Routes are declared with the `@application.route("<path>", methods=[...])` decorator directly on module-level functions. There are no Blueprints, no `add_url_rule`, no `url_prefix`, and no MethodView anywhere in the repo (git grep for Blueprint/add_url_rule/url_prefix/MethodView returns nothing). When `methods` is omitted Flask defaults to GET (and HEAD/OPTIONS). Multi-line decorators occur (views.py:547-550). Some routes are declared inside an `if application.debug or application.testing:` block (views.py:589 onward) and are therefore conditionally registered at runtime (test/dev only).
route_idioms.prefix_rules: No prefixes: the decorator string is the full path. The app is served at root by granian via `server.serve("snuba.web.wsgi:application", f"{host}:{port}", ...)` (snuba/cli/api.py:60-68) or `application.run(host, port)` in debug (snuba/cli/api.py:46-51); default HOST 0.0.0.0 / PORT 1218 (snuba/settings/__init__.py:26-27). snuba/web/wsgi.py:8 just re-exports `application`. Path parameters use Werkzeug syntax `<name>` (string), `<int:name>`, and three CUSTOM converters registered on the url_map: `<dataset:...>`, `<entity:...>`, `<storage:...>` (views.py:131-133, classes in snuba/web/converters.py:13-34). The converters accept any single path segment and resolve it at request time to a Dataset/Entity/Storage (names come from YAML configs under snuba/datasets/configuration/*, e.g. dataset names events, discover, transactions, search_issues, metrics, outcomes, replays, profiles, functions, group_attributes, events_analytics_platform...). For matching purposes treat them as wildcards `{dataset}`, `{entity}`, `{storage}`.
examples: snuba/web/views.py:286 @application.route("/query", methods=["GET", "POST"])  (GET redirects to f"/{settings.DEFAULT_DATASET_NAME}/query" at 290, a path with no matching route)
snuba/web/views.py:299 @application.route("/rpc/<name>/<version>", methods=["POST"])  -> POST /rpc/{name}/{version}, protobuf body; dispatched via run_rpc_handler (snuba/web/rpc/__init__.py:374-376)
snuba/web/views.py:307 @application.route("/<dataset:dataset>/snql", methods=["GET", "POST"])  -> /{dataset}/snql (main SnQL query endpoint used by sentry/snuba-sdk)
snuba/web/views.py:336 @application.route("/<storage:storage>", methods=["DELETE"])  -> DELETE /{storage} (bulk delete; single-segment catch-all)

route_idioms.framework: Snuba RPC registry (second-level dispatch behind POST /rpc/<name>/<version>)
route_idioms.how_declared: The concrete RPC 'routes' are not strings anywhere: each endpoint is a subclass of `RPCEndpoint` (snuba/web/rpc/__init__.py:103) whose metaclass `RegisteredClass` registers it under `config_key() = f"{cls.__name__}__{cls.version()}"` (rpc/__init__.py:121-122). `get_from_name(name, version)` looks up `f"{name}__{version}"` (rpc/__init__.py:133-137). Modules are auto-imported with `import_submodules_in_directory(module_path, f"snuba.web.rpc.{v}")` (rpc/__init__.py:371). So the URL segment {name} is the Python CLASS NAME and {version} is the string returned by `version()`.
route_idioms.prefix_rules: Full URL = "/rpc/" + ClassName + "/" + version(). All current endpoints return "v1". Derived concrete paths: /rpc/EndpointTraceItemTable/v1, /rpc/EndpointTimeSeries/v1, /rpc/EndpointTraceItemStats/v1, /rpc/EndpointTraceItemDetails/v1, /rpc/EndpointTraceItemAttributeNames/v1, /rpc/AttributeValuesRequest/v1, /rpc/EndpointGetTrace/v1, /rpc/EndpointGetTraces/v1, /rpc/EndpointDeleteTraceItems/v1, /rpc/EndpointExportTraceItems/v1, /rpc/CreateSubscriptionRequest/v1.

route_idioms.how_declared: Separate Flask app `application = Flask(__name__, static_url_path="/static", static_folder="dist")` (snuba/admin/views.py:84), same `@application.route(...)` decorator idiom, usually stacked with `@check_tool_perms(...)`. Served by snuba/admin/wsgi.py:9 / snuba/cli/admin.py:34-42 on ADMIN_PORT 1219 (snuba/settings/__init__.py:34). Only consumed by its own React frontend (same repo) and humans; not called by sentry/relay/symbolicator.
route_idioms.prefix_rules: No prefixes. Werkzeug `<param>` path params (plain strings).
examples: snuba/admin/views.py:990 @application.route("/rpc_execute/<endpoint_name>/<version>", methods=["POST"]) (calls run_rpc_handler in-process, not over HTTP)

extractor_notes:
Summary for the answer key: snuba is a SERVER-side endpoint in the cross-service graph. Within this tree I found no code-level outbound HTTP call from snuba to sentry, relay or symbolicator. Every client call site targets ClickHouse, Slack, GitHub, GoCD, Google IAP certs, or snuba-admin's own backend. The one exception is sentry_sdk event reporting via DSN (snuba/environment.py:181), which is runtime-only and usually excluded. Cross-repo edges into snuba therefore come from sentry (snuba_sdk / sentry.utils.snuba) calling /{dataset}/snql, /{dataset}/mql, /rpc/{Name}/v1, /{dataset}/{entity}/subscriptions, DELETE /{dataset}/{entity}/subscriptions/{partition}/{key}, DELETE /{storage}, /query, /health, and the /tests/... routes (used by sentry's test harness; registered only when debug/testing).

EASY (single-file, purely syntactic):
- Python decorator `decorated_definition > decorator > call(attribute(object=identifier 'application', attr 'route'))` with a string first argument and an optional `methods=[...]` keyword list. Handle decorators that span several lines (views.py:547-550, admin/views.py:225-228). Handle stacked decorators: @util.time_request at views.py:287 and @check_tool_perms in the admin app. Use GET as the default when `methods` is absent.
- Normalize Werkzeug params: `<name>`, `<int:partition>`, and the custom converters `<dataset:dataset>`, `<entity:entity>`, `<storage:storage>` become `{name}` wildcards. The converters are registered via `application.url_map.converters[...]` (views.py:131-133). Each one matches a single segment, so treat it like the default string converter.
- No prefixes or blueprints exist, so the decorator string is the full path. The extractor only needs to tag which Flask app a route belongs to: snuba/web/views.py:128 is the public API on port 1218, snuba/admin/views.py:84 is the internal admin on port 1219. Only the former is a cross-service target. Key the app by the module that defines `application`, or by the wsgi entrypoint string "snuba.web.wsgi:application" (snuba/cli/api.py:61).
- Literal-URL client calls such as requests.get/post("https://...") are trivial, but none of them point at the four services.

NEEDS CROSS-FILE OR SEMANTIC RESOLUTION:
- RPC endpoints: the HTTP route is the generic `/rpc/<name>/<version>` (views.py:299). The concrete names exist only as Python class names of `RPCEndpoint` subclasses plus the string returned by `version()`, registered through a metaclass (rpc/__init__.py:103-137) and an auto-importer (rpc/__init__.py:371). An extractor that wants concrete edges such as sentry -> /rpc/EndpointTraceItemTable/v1 must:
  - find every class whose bases include `RPCEndpoint[...]` (subscript generic base, sometimes on a wrapped line, e.g. create_subscription.py:15-17, trace_item_attribute_values.py:228-230);
  - read the `return "v1"` inside `def version`;
  - synthesize `/rpc/{ClassName}/{version}`.
  This is doable with tree-sitter but is a snuba-specific rule. On the sentry side, callers usually name the endpoint by class/proto name through a helper and do not use literal URL strings, so matching also needs a rule there.
- Conditional registration: the /tests/* routes sit inside `if application.debug or application.testing:` (views.py ~589). A purely syntactic extractor will find them, which is fine, but they should be flagged as test-only.
- ClickHouse client URLs come from settings dicts (settings/__init__.py:99-100 -> clusters/cluster.py:514) and Rust format! strings (writer_v2.rs:283). Resolving them needs settings and env propagation, but they are irrelevant to the four-service graph and should be classified as external (ClickHouse).

ONLY KNOWABLE AT RUNTIME:
- Which values the dataset, entity and storage segments accept: they come from YAML configs under snuba/datasets/configuration and the EntityKey/StorageKey enums, resolved by the converters at request time (converters.py:13-34). An extractor should match them as wildcards rather than enumerate them.
- The GET /query handler redirects to f"/{settings.DEFAULT_DATASET_NAME}/query" (views.py:290; DEFAULT_DATASET_NAME="events" at settings:86). No route serves /{dataset}/query, so this redirect is dead. Do not create an edge from it.
- sentry_sdk DSN target (settings.SENTRY_DSN), env-provided GO_SERVER_URL and ADMIN_URL, and the admin region URLs built in admin/views.py:1053 (f"https://snuba-admin{subdomain}.getsentry.net/"). That last one is returned as JSON data, not requested.
- Rust: rust_snuba runs no HTTP server. hyper and reqwest in rust_snuba/Cargo.toml:32,49 are only used for the ClickHouse writer, and the TcpListener at writer_v2.rs:766 is inside a test.

Likely misses or false positives: the admin frontend fetch() calls (api_client.tsx) match the admin routes inside the same repo, so filter out intra-repo edges. A naive "any string starting with /api/0/" scan would pick up querylog fixture strings in rust_snuba/src/processors/querylog.rs:330,439,548, which are test data, not calls.

route_idioms.framework: axum 0.8 (Rust), served via axum_server; production HTTP API of the symbolicator binary
route_idioms.how_declared: Method-chained builder on axum::Router in a single function, crates/symbolicator/src/endpoints/mod.rs::create_app. Each route is `.route("<literal path>", <method_fn>(<handler>))`. The method helpers `get`/`post` come from `axum::routing` (imported at mod.rs:3). One route uses a chained second method (`get(proxy).head(proxy)`). Handlers are imported under local aliases (mod.rs:24-31, e.g. `use proxy::proxy_symstore_request as proxy;`), so the identifier in `.route()` is an alias, not the real fn name. The handler's real path and query parameters are taken in the handler signature through extractors: `extract::Path<T>` (requests.rs:17, proxy.rs:47), `extract::Query<T>` (symbolicate.rs:58), `extract::Json<T>` (symbolicate.rs:59), `extract::Multipart` (minidump.rs:20, applecrashreport.rs:18). Path-parameter syntax is axum 0.8 brace style: `{name}` for one segment and `{*name}` for a catch-all wildcard.
route_idioms.prefix_rules: There are no prefixes and no `.nest()` in production code. Three sub-routers (symbolicate_router mod.rs:47-54, large_file_router mod.rs:58-63, misc_router mod.rs:66-68) are combined with `Router::new().merge(..)` (mod.rs:70-73). `merge` adds no prefix, so every path is the literal string at the root. `.layer(DefaultBodyLimit::max(..))` changes only body limits. `/healthcheck` is added after `.layer(middleware)` (mod.rs:77) so it skips the middleware but keeps the same path. The app is mounted at the root of the bound socket: server.rs:47 `endpoints::create_app(service).into_make_service()`, then server.rs:53 `axum_server::from_tcp(socket_http).serve(svc.clone())`. The bind address comes from config `bind` (server.rs:49). Full served route set: POST /symbolicate-any, POST /symbolicate-js, POST /symbolicate-jvm, POST /symbolicate, POST /applecrashreport (multipart), POST /minidump (multipart), GET+HEAD /proxy/{*path}, GET /requests/{request_id}, GET /healthcheck. Sentry is the caller of these routes: sentry src/sentry/lang/native/symbolicator.py:259/277/308/321/365/412/453 pass "symbolicate-any", "minidump", "applecrashreport", "symbolicate", "symbolicate-js", "symbolicate-jvm" to `self._process(...)`, and symbolicator.py:606 builds `f"requests/{task_id}"`.
examples: crates/symbolicator/src/endpoints/requests.rs:15-18 pub async fn poll_request(extract::State(service).., extract::Path(request_id): extract::Path<RequestId>, extract::Query(query)..)

route_idioms.framework: axum test/dev-only routers (not part of the production service)
route_idioms.how_declared: The same `Router::new().route(..)` style, plus `.nest_service("/prefix", ServeDir)` for static file trees. symbolicli runs an in-process local server that imitates Sentry's artifact-lookup endpoint. The symbolicator-test crate runs mock servers that imitate Sentry, the Microsoft symbol server and others.
route_idioms.prefix_rules: `.nest_service(prefix, svc)` puts the prefix in front of everything the static service serves. Those paths come from the filesystem and cannot be found statically. These routers bind to 127.0.0.1 on port 0 (random port). Their URLs are built with `index.url("lookup")` or `server.url(path)` (`format!("http://localhost:{}/{}", port, path)` at symbolicator-test/src/lib.rs:284). They imitate Sentry routes such as /lookup and /files/dsyms/ but are fakes, so the answer key and the extractor must exclude them.
examples: crates/symbolicator-test/src/lib.rs:440 url: server.url("/files/dsyms/") (fake Sentry dsym endpoint)

client_idioms.library: reqwest 0.12 async (workspace git fork getsentry/reqwest, Cargo.toml:38). The client is built by symbolicator_service::utils::http::create_client, which wraps reqwest::ClientBuilder
client_idioms.how_url_is_built: For the main inter-service link, symbolicator -> sentry, the URL comes entirely from the request payload. Sentry sends a symbol source `{"type":"sentry","url":...,"token":...}`, deserialized into `SourceConfig::Sentry(SentrySourceConfig)` (symbolicator-sources/src/sources.rs:58 `#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]`, :71 `Sentry(Arc<SentrySourceConfig>)`; SentrySourceConfig.url is a `url::Url` at symbolicator-sources/src/sources/sentry.rs:16). The /symbolicate-js body takes a single `source: SentrySourceConfig` (symbolicator/src/endpoints/symbolicate_js.rs:19). Symbolicator then only appends query pairs to that opaque URL with `Url::query_pairs_mut().append_pair(..)` and sends GET. There are four call sites. (1) Debug-file index listing: download/sentry.rs:173-185 clones `source.url` and appends `debug_id` and `code_id`; the GET is at sentry.rs:139 and `.send()` at :148. (2) Debug-file download: SentryRemoteFile::new at symbolicator-sources/src/sources/sentry.rs:56-59 appends `id=<file_id>`, and download/sentry.rs:264 runs `self.client.get(url)`. (3) JS artifact lookup: symbolicator-js/src/api_lookup.rs:113-131 appends `release`, `url` (repeated), `dist` and `debug_id` to source.url, then calls `SentryDownloader::fetch_sentry_json` at :159. Lookup results carry absolute URLs, and api_lookup.rs:224-234 `make_remote_file` sends credentials only if `url.starts_with(source.url)`. (4) Attachment download: download/sentry.rs:280, where the URL is the `storage_url` from the /symbolicate-any body (symbolicate_any.rs:38/43, wrapped by symbolicator-native/src/symbolication/attachments.rs:26). That storage_url is a pre-signed Objectstore URL (sentry src/sentry/objectstore/__init__.py:247 get_internal_download_url), so it is NOT one of the four repos. Auth is the `authenticate()` helper at sentry.rs:305-310, either a bearer token or a Cookie header. On the Sentry side, the URLs symbolicator calls are built from Django `reverse()`. sentry src/sentry/lang/native/sources.py:349-358 does `get_internal_url_prefix() + reverse("sentry-api-0-dsym-files")`, which is route src/sentry/api/urls.py:3039-3041 `^{org}/{project}/files/dsyms/$`. sources.py:379-387 does the same with reverse("sentry-api-0-project-artifact-lookup"), which is urls.py:3219-3221 `^{org}/{project}/artifact-lookup/$`.
client_idioms.base_url_config: Runtime only. The base URL is whatever sentry puts into the request JSON (`sources[].url` / `source.url`). No symbolicator config file contains a Sentry base URL. Clients are built in DownloadService::new (download/mod.rs:147-192, sentry client settings at :170-173 with connect_to_reserved_ips: true), all via utils/http.rs:88 `create_client`.
examples: crates/symbolicator-js/src/api_lookup.rs:113 let mut lookup_url = source.url.clone(); (query pairs added at :115-130)

extractor_notes:
Routes, easy case. Every production route sits in one function (crates/symbolicator/src/endpoints/mod.rs:38-78). A tree-sitter-rust query can match a `call_expression` whose callee is `field_expression` with field `route` (receiver chain rooted at `Router::new()`). The first arg is a `string_literal` path. The second arg is a call whose function identifier is get/post/put/delete/patch/head/options. That call can itself be the receiver of a further `.head(...)` / `.post(...)` method chain (mod.rs:67), so walk the method chain to collect every HTTP method. `.merge(x)` adds no prefix, so take paths literally. Still resolve `x` back to its `let x = Router::new()...` binding in the same function so routes on sub-routers are not lost. To find the handler function, resolve the `use ... as alias` lines at mod.rs:24-31; the identifier in `.route()` is the alias. Path params: `{name}` and `{*name}` (axum 0.8). Normalize them to a common placeholder so they match the Sentry side (for example requests/{task_id}). If a future version uses `.nest("/p", r)`, concatenate the prefix. `.nest_service` with ServeDir serves filesystem-derived paths and cannot be enumerated.

Routes to exclude. Routers in `crates/*/tests/**`, in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, in crates/symbolicator-test, and in crates/symbolicli/src/js_local_source.rs (a local fake of Sentry's /lookup, bound to 127.0.0.1:0). Several of these fake Sentry endpoints (`/files/dsyms/`, `/lookup`), so including them would create false sentry<->symbolicator matches. Production can be told apart by crate: only `crates/symbolicator` is the server binary. A useful heuristic: the router is reached from a fn called by `axum_server::from_tcp(..).serve(..)` (server.rs:47-53).

Outbound calls, the hard case. The real cross-service traffic is symbolicator -> sentry (dsym index listing, dsym download, JS artifact-lookup). In the service code it is fully runtime-determined. The call sites are `client.get(<Url variable>)` at download/sentry.rs:139/264/280. The Url comes from `SentrySourceConfig.url`, which serde deserializes from the request JSON that Sentry sends. The only static operations are `query_pairs_mut().append_pair(..)`, which change query strings, not the path. A tree-sitter extractor can find these `client.get(x)` / `.send()` calls and tag them "base URL from request body field `url` of a `type: sentry` source". It cannot recover a path from symbolicator alone. To link them, you need a cross-repo rule: sentry builds that URL with `get_internal_url_prefix() + reverse("sentry-api-0-dsym-files")` (sentry src/sentry/lang/native/sources.py:349-358, urls.py:3039) and `reverse("sentry-api-0-project-artifact-lookup")` (sources.py:379-388, urls.py:3219). Then it passes the URL as a JSON field to symbolicator. In other words, the edge is sentry-route-URL -> payload -> symbolicator GET. An extractor should either emit these as synthetic edges from a hand-written rule, or follow the URL as a value through the HTTP payload (very hard).

Medium case, statically resolvable with local data flow. symbolicli builds URLs with `base_url.join(&format!("projects/{org}/{project}/..."))` (main.rs:227, 273, 381, 421, 468). The format string literal gives the path template. It is relative to a base that settings.rs:262 joined with "/api/0/", so resolving it means tracing `base_url` through the `EventKey`/`Mode::Online` struct fields across functions in the same crate. Treat `{org}` etc. inside format! as path params. Note `Url::join` semantics: a leading "/" replaces the path, and no leading slash appends relative to the last "/". The literal on the second join (main.rs:421) is relative to the attachments URL. symbolicli is a developer CLI, not a deployed service, so decide whether such edges belong in the answer key (they hit real sentry routes: urls.py:2994, 3004, 3014, 3039, 3219).

Easy but intra-repo. healthcheck.rs:15 `format!("http://{addr}/healthcheck")` and process-event main.rs:58/69 `format!("{symbolicator}/minidump"|"/symbolicate")` are literal format strings and easy to extract. They target symbolicator itself, so they are not inter-service edges.

Ignore. reqwest calls to S3/GCS/Azure/HTTP symbol servers, the shared cache, JS scraping and Objectstore storage_url. All their URLs come from runtime config or payloads and none reaches relay, snuba or sentry routes.

Inbound edges to symbolicator are best found from the caller side. Sentry src/sentry/lang/native/symbolicator.py passes bare path strings ("symbolicate", "symbolicate-js", "symbolicate-jvm", "symbolicate-any", "minidump", "applecrashreport", f"requests/{task_id}") to a `_process`/`_request` wrapper (symbolicator.py:602, 606-609) that prepends a configured symbolicator base URL. That needs cross-function resolution on the Python side, not in symbolicator.

Relay and snuba. Symbolicator makes no HTTP calls to either (grep for snuba/relay in crates/**/*.rs finds only comments), and neither appears as a caller in symbolicator code.
